headline: Massachusetts urges consumers to check generic-drug settlement claims
dek: People who bought certain generic drugs from 2009 through 2019 may be eligible for compensation from multistate settlements totaling about $96.5 million.
body: Massachusetts consumers who bought certain generic drugs between May 2009 and December 2019 may be eligible to claim compensation from multistate settlements, the Massachusetts Attorney General’s Office said Wednesday.

The U.S. District Court for the District of Connecticut this month gave preliminary approval to a plan filed by Massachusetts and a coalition of 47 other states and territories to distribute settlement funds paid by generic-drug manufacturers. The plan addresses claims that the companies illegally coordinated to raise prices.

The coalition previously announced settlements with Glenmark, Lannett, Bausch, Apotex, Heritage and Heritage’s parent company, Emcure, totaling about $96.5 million. Massachusetts, which filed its lawsuit in December 2025, is set to receive $1.9 million as part of the settlement.

Consumers can review the covered-drug list and eligibility information at AGGenericDrugs.com, or contact the claims administrator at 1-866-290-0182 or info@AGGenericDrugs.com. The Attorney General’s notice says purchasers should use those resources to determine whether they qualify and submit a claim.
author: NorthEast News Desk
